comments.body: Owner decision (Travis, 2026-10-13): suspend remembered prefix approvals from a less strict level while Aggressive is active (they must not auto-approve under Aggressive). Implementing.

Fixed in #661, merged as 4b6dd55c85 (PR head 8666aeb40a). This implements Travis's 2026-10-13 decision.

**What changed**
- **Under Aggressive, only approvals saved under Aggressive apply.** A "Yes, and don't ask again for commands that start with …" rule auto-approves only if a person saved it while Aggressive was active.
  - Such rules are now saved in the Corbanu home's `rules/default.rules` with the justification `Remembered while security level Aggressive was active.`.
  - Only that file is trusted to carry the mark. A project's `.codex/rules` cannot claim it.
- **Every other `allow` rule is suspended, not deleted.** That includes rules from admin or system layers.
- **The person is asked, and told why.** The prompt's Reason says: "A remembered approval (don't ask again for commands that start with `…`) was not applied because security level Aggressive is on … They are kept and apply again when you return to a less strict level." A rejected prompt says the same.
- **Choosing "don't ask again" under Aggressive** saves a marked rule. It then applies under Aggressive and under Permissive.
- **Permissive and Moderate are unchanged.**

**Evidence**
- **Regression tests:** `core/tests/suite/issue_626.rs` fails before the fix and passes after it, with real Seatbelt on macOS and real bubblewrap on glitch.
- **Unit tests:** `exec_policy::aggressive::tests`.
- **Focused `just test` and clippy:** `just test` passes with and without developer-accounting, and clippy `-D warnings` is clean on macOS and Linux.
- **Review:** an independent review ended in APPROVE.
- **G11b replay** (tmux, GLM 5.3 Flash): I approved "don't ask again" under Permissive, switched to Aggressive and ran the same command.
  - It asked again and showed the note.
  - The rule was still in `default.rules`.
  - Screens: `qa/security-levels/fixes/issue-623-626-20261013/replay-g11b.txt`.
- **Video:** https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/releases/download/demos/issue-626-issue626-remembered-approval-suspended-79e5ab0c0b26-2026-10-13.mp4

**Known gap:** commands intercepted by zsh-fork are suspended the same way, but their prompt doesn't show the note. zsh-fork is off by default.
Owner decision (Travis, 2026-10-13): add the 'remembered approval not applied' note for zsh-fork-intercepted commands too, so it appears whenever zsh-fork is on.

The 2026-10-13 decision is implemented in #728 (merged as 028833042f, head 359a17f100): the "remembered approval was not applied" note now also appears for commands intercepted by zsh-fork, whenever zsh-fork is on.

**What changed**
- With zsh-fork on, a program that a command's script starts is checked when it starts, through both the shell tool and unified exec.
- Under Aggressive, if a suspended remembered approval would have run that program unasked, its prompt carries the same note as a shell command's prompt. When the approval policy refuses to ask, the refusal says it too.
- Decisions are unchanged: the same programs are suspended and prompted. Permissive, Moderate and zsh-fork off are unchanged.

**Evidence**
- **Tests:** `core/tests/suite/issue_626.rs`, `issue_626_zsh_fork_prompt_names_the_suspended_approval` and its unified-exec variant. They use a real zsh-fork runtime and Seatbelt, and fail without the fix.
- **Focused `just test`:** passes with and without developer-accounting.
  - Two zsh-fork tests fail the same way on main on this Mac: `skill_approval::shell_zsh_fork_skill_scripts_ignore_declared_permissions` and `unified_exec_zsh_fork_approvals::unified_exec_zsh_fork_parent_approval_preserves_denied_reads`.
- **Clippy `-D warnings`:** clean on macOS and Linux (glitch), and Windows clippy passed.
- **Review:** an independent Opus 5.5 High review approved, then approved again after a nit fix and on the QA-only head.
- **tmux check** (GLM 5.3 Flash):
  - Under Permissive, "don't ask again" was approved for `touch remembered.txt`.
  - Under Aggressive, `f=remembered.txt; touch "$f"` was run. The intercepted `/usr/bin/touch remembered.txt` prompt showed the note.
  - Record: `qa/security-levels/fixes/issue-626-zsh-fork-20261013/`.
- **Video:** https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/releases/download/demos/issue-626-issue626-zsh-fork-remembered-approval-note-98ba145fa017-2026-10-13.mp4

title: Aggressive (AGG-33 replay): a "don't ask again" prefix rule approved under Permissive still auto-approves after switching to Aggressive
